question.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{10}{3}x{y}^{4}, & 1\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Find $P(Y<\frac{4}{5}).$
question.worked_solution:
If $X$ and $Y$ are two continuous random variables with joint probability density function $f(x,y),$ then the marginal density functions for $X$ and $Y$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}y,\,{f}_{Y}(y)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, the marginal density function of $Y$ for $0\le y\le 1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(y) & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{10}{3}x{y}^{4}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{10}{3}{y}^{4}{[\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}]}_{x=1}^{x=2} \\  & =\frac{5}{3}{y}^{4}({2}^{2}-{1}^{2}) \\  & =5{y}^{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the full expression for ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is given by

$$
{f}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}5{y}^{4}, & 0\le y\le 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required probability is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y<\frac{4}{5}) & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{4/5}{f}_{Y}(y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4/5}5{y}^{4}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={[{y}^{5}]}_{0}^{4/5} \\  & ={(\frac{4}{5})}^{5}-{0}^{5} \\  & =\frac{1024}{3125}.\end{aligned}
$$
